problem.summary: 传统GAN生成器架构将潜在码直接输入输入层，导致潜在空间中的变化因素不可避免地纠缠，且难以实现对生成图像的高分辨率细节和全局属性的独立控制。

motivation.summary: 借鉴风格迁移文献，提出一种新的生成器架构，以实现对生成图像的高层属性（如姿态、身份）和随机变化（如雀斑、头发）的自动、无监督分离，并实现直观的、尺度特定的控制。

core_idea.summary: 将输入潜在码映射到一个中间潜在空间W，该空间不受训练数据概率密度的限制，从而允许更解耦的表示。通过自适应实例归一化（AdaIN）将W中的风格注入合成网络的每一层，并通过显式噪声输入提供随机细节。

method.summary: 提出基于风格的生成器架构，包含映射网络f和合成网络g。映射网络将输入潜在码z映射到中间潜在空间w。合成网络通过AdaIN操作在每一卷积层后注入风格y，并通过添加高斯噪声输入提供随机变化。引入混合正则化以提高风格的局部化。

experiments.summary: 在CelebA-HQ、FFHQ、LSUN BEDROOM、LSUN CAR等数据集上进行实验。使用Fréchet起始距离（FID）评估生成质量。提出感知路径长度和线性可分性两个新指标来量化插值质量和解耦程度。进行消融研究（Table 1）和混合正则化测试（Table 2）。

claims.claim: 基于风格的生成器架构在传统分布质量指标（FID）上优于传统生成器。
新架构能自动学习高层属性和随机变化的无监督分离。
中间潜在空间W比输入潜在空间Z具有更线性、更少纠缠的表示。
混合正则化能提高风格的局部化，从而改善对多个潜在码混合的容忍度。
噪声输入仅影响随机变化，不影响全局属性。
基于风格的生成器架构在所有方面都优于传统生成器架构。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论该架构在非人脸数据集上的泛化能力。混合正则化可能会略微扭曲中间潜在空间W。训练时间较长（约一周）。未探索该架构作为正则化器的潜力。

nodes.title: 输入潜在码z
nodes.label: Input Latent Code
nodes.summary: 从标准正态分布或均匀分布中采样的初始潜在向量。
nodes.description: 传统GAN的输入潜在码，其分布必须匹配训练数据的概率密度，这可能导致纠缠。

nodes.title: 映射网络f
nodes.label: Mapping Network
nodes.summary: 一个由8个全连接层组成的网络，将输入潜在码z映射到中间潜在空间W。
nodes.description: 映射网络f将z映射到w，其目的是“解开”W，使得变化因素更加线性。该网络使用较小的学习率（λ' = 0.01·λ）以稳定训练。

nodes.title: 中间潜在空间W
nodes.label: Intermediate Latent Space
nodes.summary: 映射网络的输出空间，其分布不受训练数据限制，允许更解耦的表示。
nodes.description: W空间是自由的，不受输入潜在空间Z必须匹配训练数据密度的限制，因此可以更解耦。风格y是从w通过仿射变换A得到的。

nodes.title: 仿射变换A
nodes.label: Affine Transform
nodes.summary: 将中间潜在码w转换为风格向量y = (ys, yb)的线性变换。
nodes.description: 仿射变换A将w映射到风格y，y包含缩放因子ys和偏置yb，用于控制AdaIN操作。

nodes.title: 合成网络g
nodes.label: Synthesis Network
nodes.summary: 由18层组成的网络（每个分辨率2层），通过AdaIN和噪声输入生成图像。
nodes.description: 合成网络g接收风格y和噪声输入，通过AdaIN操作在每一卷积层后注入风格，并通过添加高斯噪声提供随机细节。从常量输入（4×4×512）开始。

nodes.title: 自适应实例归一化（AdaIN）
nodes.label: Adaptive Instance Normalization
nodes.summary: 一种操作，对每个特征图进行归一化，然后使用风格y进行缩放和偏置。
nodes.description: AdaIN(xi, y) = ys,i * (xi - μ(xi)) / σ(xi) + yb,i。它将风格y注入到合成网络的每一层。

nodes.title: 噪声输入
nodes.label: Noise Inputs
nodes.summary: 单通道高斯噪声图像，通过学习的缩放因子B添加到合成网络的每一层。
nodes.description: 噪声输入提供随机细节（如头发、雀斑），不影响全局属性。噪声在卷积后、非线性前添加。

nodes.title: 混合正则化
nodes.label: Mixing Regularization
nodes.summary: 一种训练技术，在训练期间以一定概率使用两个不同的潜在码生成图像，以提高风格的局部化。
nodes.description: 在训练期间，以一定百分比（如90%）的样本使用两个随机潜在码z1, z2，并随机选择交叉点来混合风格。这提高了网络对多个潜在码混合的容忍度。

nodes.title: 生成图像
nodes.label: Generated Image
nodes.summary: 合成网络的输出，分辨率为1024×1024。
nodes.description: 最终生成的图像，其质量通过FID评估。图像展示了高层属性和随机变化的分离。

edges.label: 映射
edges.description: 输入潜在码z被输入到映射网络f中。

edges.label: 输出
edges.description: 映射网络f输出中间潜在码w。

edges.label: 变换
edges.description: 中间潜在码w通过仿射变换A转换为风格y。

edges.label: 注入
edges.description: AdaIN将风格注入合成网络g的每一层。

edges.label: 添加
edges.description: 噪声输入被添加到合成网络g的每一层。

edges.label: 生成
edges.description: 合成网络g生成最终图像。

edges.label: 正则化
edges.description: 混合正则化在训练期间影响映射网络f和合成网络g的输入。

deltas.before: 潜在码z直接输入生成器的输入层。
deltas.after: 潜在码z先通过映射网络f映射到中间潜在空间W，然后通过仿射变换A转换为风格y，再通过AdaIN注入合成网络的每一层。
deltas.why_it_matters: 中间潜在空间W不受训练数据分布的限制，允许更解耦的表示，从而实现高层属性和随机变化的分离，并改善插值质量。

deltas.before: 生成器没有显式的随机细节输入机制。
deltas.after: 在合成网络的每一层添加高斯噪声输入，通过学习的缩放因子B进行缩放。
deltas.why_it_matters: 噪声输入提供随机细节（如头发、雀斑），而不影响全局属性（如身份、姿态），实现了随机变化的局部化控制。

deltas.after: 在训练期间引入混合正则化，以一定概率使用两个不同的潜在码生成图像，并随机选择交叉点来混合风格。
deltas.why_it_matters: 提高了风格的局部化，使网络对多个潜在码混合的容忍度更高，从而改善了FID。

deltas.after: 使用双线性上/下采样，并在每次上采样后和下采样前应用低通滤波。
deltas.why_it_matters: 提高了基线生成器的质量（FID从7.79降至6.11）。

deltas.after: 对于FFHQ数据集，使用非饱和损失和R1正则化。
deltas.why_it_matters: R1正则化使得FID在更长的训练时间内持续下降，因此将训练时间从12M图像增加到25M图像。

variables.name: x_i
variables.description: 合成网络中某一层的第i个特征图。

variables.name: y
variables.description: 风格向量，包含缩放因子y_s和偏置y_b。

formulas.intuition: 自适应实例归一化操作，对每个特征图进行归一化，然后使用风格y进行缩放和偏置，从而将风格注入到合成网络的每一层。

formulas.formula: l_Z = \mathbb{E} \left[ \frac{1}{\epsilon^2} d(G(\text{slerp}(z_1, z_2; t)), G(\text{slerp}(z_1, z_2; t + \epsilon))) \right]

variables.name: l_Z
variables.description: 输入潜在空间Z中的平均感知路径长度。

variables.name: z_1, z_2
variables.description: 从输入潜在分布P(z)中采样的两个潜在码。

variables.name: t
variables.description: 插值参数，服从均匀分布U(0,1)。

variables.name: G
variables.description: 生成器，对于基于风格的网络是g∘f。

formulas.intuition: 衡量在输入潜在空间Z中沿球面线性插值路径的感知变化。路径越短，表示潜在空间越平滑、越线性。

formulas.formula: l_W = \mathbb{E} \left[ \frac{1}{\epsilon^2} d(g(\text{lerp}(f(z_1), f(z_2); t)), g(\text{lerp}(f(z_1), f(z_2); t + \epsilon))) \right]

variables.name: l_W
variables.description: 中间潜在空间W中的平均感知路径长度。

formulas.intuition: 衡量在中间潜在空间W中沿线性插值路径的感知变化。由于W不受输入分布限制，路径通常更短，表示更解耦的表示。

variables.name: \bar{w}
variables.description: W空间的中心质量，即平均脸。

formulas.intuition: 截断技巧在W空间中的应用。通过将风格向量w向平均脸\bar{w}收缩，可以生成更典型、质量更高的图像，但会牺牲多样性。

variables.name: H(Y_i | X_i)
variables.description: 给定线性SVM预测X_i时，属性Y_i的条件熵。

formulas.intuition: 线性可分性分数，衡量潜在空间中属性的可分离程度。分数越低，表示潜在空间越解耦。

main_result.description: 在CelebA-HQ和FFHQ数据集上，比较不同生成器架构的FID。
main_result.result: 基于风格的生成器（配置E）在FFHQ上的FID为4.42，优于传统生成器（配置B）的5.25。

main_result.experiment: 感知路径长度和线性可分性（Table 3）
main_result.description: 在FFHQ数据集上，测量不同生成器架构的感知路径长度和线性可分性分数。
main_result.result: 基于风格的生成器（配置E）在W空间中的路径长度（200.5）远低于传统生成器在Z空间中的路径长度（412.0），且可分性分数更低（3.54 vs 10.78）。

ablation.description: 逐步添加组件（映射网络、风格、噪声输入、混合正则化）并观察FID变化。
ablation.result: 每个组件都带来了FID的改善。从基线B到风格化生成器E，FID从5.25降至4.42。

ablation.description: 研究映射网络深度对FID、路径长度和可分性的影响。
ablation.result: 更深的映射网络（8层）通常带来更好的FID、更短的路径长度和更低的可分性分数。

robustness.description: 在测试时使用多个随机潜在码（1-4个）和随机交叉点，评估网络对混合的容忍度。
robustness.result: 混合正则化（如90%）显著提高了网络对多个潜在码混合的容忍度，FID从17.41降至9.03（使用4个潜在码时）。

scaling.experiment: 训练过程中的指标变化（Figure 9）
scaling.description: 观察FID和感知路径长度随训练图像数量的变化。
scaling.result: FID随着训练时间的增加而持续下降，但路径长度略有上升，表明FID的改善可能以更纠缠的表示为代价。

case_study.description: 从两个源潜在码生成图像，并通过复制特定尺度的风格来混合。
case_study.result: 粗尺度风格控制高层属性（如姿态、脸型），中尺度风格控制中等特征（如眼睛开闭），细尺度风格控制颜色和细节。

case_study.description: 展示噪声输入对生成图像的影响。
case_study.result: 噪声仅影响随机细节（如头发、背景），不影响全局属性（如身份、姿态）。不同层的噪声影响不同尺度的细节。

case_study.description: 展示在W空间中应用截断技巧的效果。
case_study.result: 随着ψ减小，人脸收敛到“平均脸”。负缩放产生“反脸”，其中许多高级属性翻转。

claims.claim: 基于风格的生成器架构在传统分布质量指标（FID）上优于传统生成器。

evidence.description: 在FFHQ数据集上，基于风格的生成器（配置E）的FID为4.42，优于传统生成器（配置B）的5.25。

claims.claim: 新架构能自动学习高层属性和随机变化的无监督分离。
claims.evidence_source_type: 定性分析（Figure 3, 4, 5）和定量指标（感知路径长度、线性可分性）

evidence.description: 风格混合实验（Figure 3）显示粗尺度风格控制高层属性，细尺度风格控制细节。
随机变化实验（Figure 4, 5）显示噪声仅影响随机细节，不影响全局属性。
定量指标显示基于风格的生成器在W空间中的路径长度更短，线性可分性分数更低。

terms.term: 基于风格的生成器（Style-Based Generator）
terms.definition: 本文提出的生成器架构，包含映射网络和合成网络，通过AdaIN注入风格，并通过噪声输入添加随机细节。
一个由8个全连接层组成的网络，将输入潜在码z映射到中间潜在空间W。

terms.term: 中间潜在空间W（Intermediate Latent Space W）
terms.definition: 映射网络的输出空间，其分布不受训练数据限制，允许更解耦的表示。
一种操作，对每个特征图进行归一化，然后使用风格y进行缩放和偏置，从而将风格注入到合成网络的每一层。
从中间潜在码w通过仿射变换得到的向量y = (ys, yb)，用于控制AdaIN操作。
单通道高斯噪声图像，通过学习的缩放因子添加到合成网络的每一层，提供随机细节。
一种训练技术，在训练期间以一定概率使用两个不同的潜在码生成图像，并随机选择交叉点来混合风格，以提高风格的局部化。

terms.term: 感知路径长度（Perceptual Path Length）
terms.definition: 衡量在潜在空间中沿插值路径的感知变化的指标。路径越短，表示潜在空间越平滑、越线性。
衡量潜在空间中属性可分离程度的指标。分数越低，表示潜在空间越解耦。
在W空间中，通过将风格向量w向平均脸收缩来生成更典型、质量更高的图像的技术。
本文引入的一个新的、高质量、高多样性的人脸数据集。

steps.description: 1. 准备数据集：下载并预处理CelebA-HQ、FFHQ、LSUN BEDROOM、LSUN CAR数据集。
2. 实现基线生成器：基于Progressive GAN的官方TensorFlow实现。
3. 实现基于风格的生成器：添加映射网络、AdaIN操作、噪声输入和混合正则化。
4. 训练模型：使用R1正则化和非饱和损失（对于FFHQ），训练25M图像。
5. 评估：计算FID、感知路径长度和线性可分性分数。
6. 进行消融研究：逐步添加组件并观察性能变化。
7. 可视化：进行风格混合、随机变化和截断技巧的实验。

metadata.title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks
metadata.paper_type: Generative Models / GAN / Top-cited ML method paper
metadata.abstract: We propose an alternative generator architecture for generative adversarial networks, borrowing from style transfer literature. The new architecture leads to an automatically learned, unsupervised separation of high-level attributes (e.g., pose and identity when trained on human faces) and stochastic variation in the generated images (e.g., freckles, hair), and it enables intuitive, scale-specific control of the synthesis. The new generator improves the state-of-the-art in terms of traditional distribution quality metrics, leads to demonstrably better interpolation properties, and also better disentangles the latent factors of variation. To quantify interpolation quality and disentanglement, we propose two new, automated methods that are applicable to any generator architecture. Finally, we introduce a new, highly varied and high-quality dataset of human faces.

anchors.text_span: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks Tero Karras NVIDIA tkarras@nvidia.com Samuli Laine NVIDIA slaine@nvidia.com Timo Aila NVIDIA taila@nvidia.com
Abstract

We propose an alternative generator architecture for generative adversarial networks, borrowing from style transfer literature. The new architecture leads to an au- tomatically learned, unsupervised separation of high-level attributes (e.g., pose and identity when trained on human faces) and stochastic variation in the generated images (e.g., freckles, hair), and it enables intuitive, scale-speciﬁc control of the synthesis. The new generator improves the state-of-the-art in terms of traditional distribution quality metrics, leads to demonstrably better interpolation proper- ties, and also better disentangles the latent factors of varia- tion. To quantify interpolation quality and disentanglement, we propose two new, automated methods that are applica- ble to any generator architecture. Finally, we introduce a new, highly varied and high-quality dataset of human faces. 1. Introduction The resolution and quality of images produced by gen- erative methods — especially generative adversar...
not modify the discriminator or the loss function in any

way, and our work is thus orthogonal to the ongoing discus- sion about GAN loss functions, regularization, and hyper- parameters [24, 45, 5, 40, 44, 36]. Our generator embeds the input latent code into an inter- mediate latent space, which has a profound effect on how the factors of variation are represented in the network. The input latent space must follow the probability density of the
training data, and we argue that this leads to some degree of

unavoidable entanglement. Our intermediate latent space is free from that restriction and is therefore allowed to be disentangled. As previous methods for estimating the de- gree of latent space disentanglement are not directly appli- cable in our case, we propose two new automated metrics — perceptual path length and linear separability — for quanti- fying these aspects of the generator. Using these metrics, we show that compared to a traditional generator architecture, our generator admits a more linear, less entangled represen- tation of different factors of variation. Finally, we present a new dataset of human faces (Flickr-Faces-HQ, FFHQ) that offers much higher qual- ity and covers considerably wider variation than existing high-resolution datasets (Appendix A). We have made this dataset publicly available, along with our source code and pre-trained networks. 1 The accompanying video can be found under the same link. 2. Linear separability If a latent space is sufﬁciently disentangled, it should be possible to ﬁnd direction vectors that consistently corre- spond to individual factors of variation. We propose another metric that quantiﬁes this effect by measuring how well the latent-space points can be separated into two distinct sets via a linear hyperplane, so that each set corresponds to a speciﬁc binary attribute of the image. In order to label the generated images, we train auxiliary classiﬁcation networks for a number of binary attributes, e.g., to distinguish male and female faces. In our tests,
the classiﬁers had the same architecture as the discrimina-

tor we use (i.e., same as in [30]), and were trained using the CELEB A-HQ dataset that retains the 40 attributes available in the original CelebA dataset. To measure the separability of one attribute, we generate 200,000 images withz∼ P (z) and classify them using the auxiliary classiﬁcation network. We then sort the samples according to classiﬁer conﬁdence and remove the least conﬁdent half, yielding 100,000 la- beled latent-space vectors. For each attribute, we ﬁt a linear SVM to predict the label based on the latent-space point —z for traditional andw for style-based — and classify the points by this plane. We then compute the conditional entropy H(Y|X) where X are the classes predicted by the SVM and Y are the classes deter-
mined by the pre-trained classiﬁer. This tells how much ad-
ditional information is required to determine the true class

of a sample, given that we know on which side of the hy- perplane it lies. A low value suggests consistent latent space directions for the corresponding factor(s) of variation. We calculate the ﬁnal separability score as exp(∑ i H(Yi|Xi)), where i enumerates the 40 attributes. Similar to the inception score [53], the exponentiation
brings the values from logarithmic to linear domain so that
they are easier to compare. Tables 3 and 4 show that W is consistently better sep- arable thanZ, suggesting a less entangled representation. 7

Furthermore, increasing the depth of the mapping network improves both image quality and separability in W, which is in line with the hypothesis that the synthesis network in- herently favors a disentangled input representation. Inter- estingly, adding a mapping network in front of a traditional generator results in severe loss of separability inZ but im- proves the situation in the intermediate latent spaceW, and the FID improves as well. This shows that even the tradi- tional generator architecture performs better when we in- troduce an intermediate latent space that does not have to follow the distribution of the training data. 5. Conclusion Based on both our results and parallel work by Chen et
al. [6], it is becoming clear that the traditional GAN gen-

erator architecture is in every way inferior to a style-based design. This is true in terms of established quality metrics, and we further believe that our investigations to the separa- tion of high-level attributes and stochastic effects, as well as the linearity of the intermediate latent space will prove fruitful in improving the understanding and controllability of GAN synthesis. We note that our average path length metric could easily be used as a regularizer during training, and perhaps some variant of the linear separability metric could act as one, too. In general, we expect that methods for directly shaping the intermediate latent space during training will provide interesting avenues for future work. 6. C. Hyperparameters and training details We build upon the ofﬁcial TensorFlow [1] implemen- tation of Progressive GANs by Karras et al. [30], from which we inherit most of the training details.3 This original setup corresponds to conﬁgurationA in Table 1. In particu-
lar, we use the same discriminator architecture, resolution-
dependent minibatch sizes, Adam [33] hyperparameters,

and exponential moving average of the generator. We en- able mirror augmentation for CelebA-HQ and FFHQ, but disable it for LSUN. Our training time is approximately one week on an NVIDIA DGX-1 with 8 Tesla V100 GPUs. For our improved baseline (B in Table 1), we make sev- eral modiﬁcations to improve the overall result quality. We replace the nearest-neighbor up/downsampling in both net- works with bilinear sampling, which we implement by low- pass ﬁltering the activations with a separable 2 nd order bi- nomial ﬁlter after each upsampling layer and before each downsampling layer [64]. We implement progressive grow- ing the same way as Karras et al. [30], but we start from 82 images instead of 42. For the FFHQ dataset, we switch from WGAN-GP to the non-saturating loss [22] with R1 regular-
ization [44] using γ = 10 . With R1 we found that the FID

scores keep decreasing for considerably longer than with WGAN-GP, and we thus increase the training time from 12M to 25M images. We use the same learning rates as Karras et al. [30] for FFHQ, but we found that setting the learning rate to 0.002 instead of 0.003 for 5122 and 10242 leads to better stability with CelebA-HQ. For our style-based generator (F in Table 1), we use leaky
ReLU [41] with α = 0 .2 and equalized learning rate [30]

for all layers. We use the same feature map counts in our convolution layers as Karras et al. [30]. Our mapping net- work consists of 8 fully-connected layers, and the dimen- sionality of all input and output activations — including z and w — is 512. We found that increasing the depth of the mapping network tends to make the training unstable with high learning rates. We thus reduce the learning rate by two orders of magnitude for the mapping network, i.e.,

The biases and noise scaling factors are initialized to zero, except for the biases associated with ys that we initialize to one. The classiﬁers used by our separability metric (Sec-
tion 4.2) have the same architecture as our discriminator ex-
cept that minibatch standard deviation [30] is disabled. We
use the learning rate of 10−3, minibatch size of 8, Adam

Training convergence
Figure 9 shows how the FID and perceptual path length

metrics evolve during the training of our conﬁgurations B and F with the FFHQ dataset. With R1 regularization active in both conﬁgurations, FID continues to slowly decrease as the training progresses, motivating our choice to increase the training time from 12M images to 25M images. Even when the training has reached the full 10242 resolution, the slowly rising path lengths indicate that the improvements in FID come at the cost of a more entangled representa- tion. Considering future work, it is an interesting question whether this is unavoidable, or if it were possible to encour- age shorter path lengths without compromising the conver- gence of FID. E.
